classification.difficultyReason: Diagnose two different failures of straight-line fitting: absence of a clear linear association and a systematic curved pattern.

inlines.text: Explain why the shown lines of best fit would

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8: paired scatter plots beneath the stem
spec.description: Two complete unnumbered scatter plots in source left-to-right order. The left has five widely scattered crosses and a gently rising proposed line; the right has eight crosses rising and flattening, with a steeper proposed line. Relative positions reconstruct the source appearance without asserting numerical data values.
spec.mathematics: The left plot has no clear linear association. The right plot follows an increasing curved pattern that a straight line does not represent.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes, cross markers and both proposed blue lines are permanent student-visible givens; explanations appear only in answers.

answer.short: Left: no clear linear association. Right: the association is curved, not linear.
answer.worked: Left: the points are widely scattered and do not follow a clear straight-line pattern, so the proposed line is not a useful fit. Right: the points rise and then flatten, showing a non-linear association; a straight line does not follow this pattern.
